items.prompt: Which of these is alive?

figure.alt: Four pictures: a goldfish, a toy car, a pebble and a kite.

options.why: A toy car can move, but it cannot grow or have young.
A pebble was never alive.
A kite moves in the wind, but it does not eat or grow.

hints: Think about which one needs food and water.
Living things grow and can have young.
Start with the goldfish. Does it eat and grow?
items.explanation: A goldfish is alive. It eats, breathes, grows and can have young.

items.prompt: Sort into alive, once alive and never alive.
hints: Once alive means it was alive before, or was part of a living thing.
Ask two questions. Is it alive now? Was it ever part of a living thing?
Start with the wooden spoon. Where does wood come from?
items.explanation: The tree, the rabbit and the ladybird are alive now. The wooden spoon, the feather and the dry leaf came from living things, so they were once alive. The stone, the key and the bottle were never alive.

items.prompt: Choose all the things that every living thing does.

options.why: Only children go to school. Trees and fish do not.
Plants and most animals cannot talk.

hints: Think about a tree, a fish and you. What do all three do?
Check each choice against a plant.
Start with grows. Does a tree grow? Does a fish grow?
items.explanation: All living things grow and need food and water. Plants make their own food. Talking and going to school are things only some living things do.

items.prompt: A wooden chair is made from a ___.

figure.alt: A tall living thing with a trunk, branches and leaves, marked with a question mark.

hints: Wood comes from a plant.
Think about a plant that grows tall and has a trunk.
Look at the lines in wood. Where did they grow?
items.explanation: Wood comes from trees. A wooden chair was once part of a living tree, so it was once alive.

items.prompt: Which one was never alive?

options.why: Cotton comes from the cotton plant, so it was once alive.
Paper is made from wood, which comes from trees.
A seashell was once part of a living sea animal.

hints: Think about where each material comes from.
Was it ever part of a plant or an animal?
Start with the cotton T-shirt. Where does cotton grow?
items.explanation: Glass is made from sand, which was never alive. Cotton, paper and shells all come from living things.

items.prompt: A puppy becomes a big dog. Which life process is this?

options.why: Moving means going from place to place.
Eating gives the puppy food. Getting bigger is a different process.
Sensing means noticing things with the senses.

hints: Think about what changes as the puppy gets older.
Which word means getting bigger?
Compare the puppy at the start with the dog at the end.
items.explanation: Getting bigger is growing. All living things grow.

items.prompt: Match each life process to an example.
hints: Each example shows one thing living things do.
Do the ones you are surest about first.
Start with moving. Which example shows going from place to place?
items.explanation: A fish swimming shows moving, and a seed becoming a plant shows growing. A cat hearing a mouse shows sensing, and a cow eating grass shows feeding. A hen laying eggs shows having young.

items.prompt: A car moves and needs fuel, like food. Why is it not alive?

options.why: Whales are huge, and they are alive.

options.text: It cannot grow or have young.
It is made in a factory.
options.why: Where it was made does not decide it. Living things grow and have young.
Cheetahs are very fast, and they are alive.

hints: Moving and using fuel are not enough.
Think about all the life processes. Which ones can a car not do?
Ask: will a car ever get bigger or have baby cars?
items.explanation: A car can move and uses fuel, but it cannot grow, sense or have young. Living things do all of these, so a car is not alive.

items.prompt: Did it come from a plant or an animal? Sort the cards.
hints: Think about where each material first came from.
Plants give us wood and cotton. Animals give us other things.
Start with wool. Which animal has woolly hair?
items.explanation: Cotton, paper and wood come from plants. Wool comes from sheep, feathers come from birds and honey is made by bees.

items.prompt: Which one is alive?

options.why: A fire can spread, but it does not feed, sense or have young.
Clouds move and change shape, but they were never alive.
A robot dog can move and bark, but it cannot grow or have young.

hints: Some living things are resting and look like they do nothing.
Ask: could it grow if it got water and warmth?
Start with the seed. What happens when you plant it?
items.explanation: A seed is alive. It rests until it gets water and warmth, then it grows into a new plant.

items.prompt: Andi finds a dry brown leaf on the ground. Which is true?

figure.alt: A dry brown leaf on the ground.

options.why: It grew on a plant, so it was once part of a living thing.
It has fallen and dried out. It cannot grow any more.

options.text: It will grow into a tree.
options.why: Leaves do not grow into trees. Seeds do.

hints: Think about where the leaf came from.
Can a dry, fallen leaf still grow?
Ask: was it ever part of a living plant?
items.explanation: The leaf grew on a living plant, so it was once alive. Now it is dry and dead, so it cannot grow.

items.prompt: Living things need ___ to breathe.
hints: You cannot see it, but it is all around you.
Hold your breath for a moment. What do you need next?
It fills a balloon when you blow into it.
items.explanation: Living things need air. Animals breathe in air, and plants take in air through their leaves.

items.prompt: Fossils are found in rock. They show animals or plants from long ago. Which is true about a fossil shell?

figure.alt: A fossil shell shape inside a piece of rock.

options.why: The animal died a very, very long time ago.
A fossil is made of rock. It cannot hatch.
The rock was never alive, but the shell shape came from a sea animal.

options.text: It came from a living thing.

hints: A fossil keeps the shape of something from long ago.
Think about what made the shell in the first place.
Ask: did a living animal once have this shell?
items.explanation: A fossil shell shows the shape of a sea animal that lived long ago. It came from a living thing, so it was once alive.

items.prompt: Choose all the things a plant does that show it is alive.

options.why: Plants stay in one place. Their roots grow towards water.
Plants do not talk.

hints: Think about what you have seen plants do.
Plants are living, but they do things slowly.
Start with growing towards the light. Have you seen a plant on a windowsill lean?
items.explanation: Plants grow towards the light, make seeds and need water. These show they are alive, even though they cannot walk or talk.

items.prompt: How many objects are made from something that was once alive?

head: Object
Material
figure.alt: Table of objects and materials: chair, wood. Spoon, metal. Scarf, wool. Window, glass. Notebook, paper. Wall, brick.

hints: Look at the material column.
For each material, ask: did it come from a plant or an animal?
Start with wood. It comes from trees, so count 1.
items.explanation: Wood comes from trees, wool comes from sheep and paper is made from wood. That makes 3. Metal, glass and brick were never alive.

items.prompt: Draw something alive, something once alive and something never alive. Label each one.

criteria.label: Draws something that is alive now
Draws something that was once alive
Draws something that was never alive
Writes a clear label for each drawing

hints: Once alive things include wood, paper and feathers.
Never alive things include stones, metal and glass.
items.explanation: A plant or a pet is alive. Wood and feathers were once alive. Stones, metal and glass were never alive.

items.prompt: A dry log was once part of a tree. What do we call it?

options.why: It no longer grows.
It came from a living tree.
It is wood, not rock.

hints: The tree grew long ago.
The log cannot grow now.
It is not a rock.
items.explanation: A log came from a living tree, but it is dead now. We say it was once alive.

items.prompt: Which one is made from something once alive?

options.why: Glass is made from sand.
Metal comes from rocks.
A stone was never alive.

hints: Paper comes from trees.
Glass and metal come from the ground.
Think about what paper is made from.
items.explanation: Paper is made from wood, which comes from trees.

items.prompt: Which living thing makes its own food using sunlight?

options.why: A dog eats food.
A fish eats food.
A bird eats food.

hints: Which one is a plant?
Animals have to find food.
Leaves catch sunlight.
items.explanation: Plants use sunlight to make their own food. Animals must eat.

items.prompt: What do living things do to make more of their kind?

options.why: Sleeping does not make new life.
Melting is a change of state.
Floating does not make new life.

hints: Think about a hen and her eggs.
Plants have seeds.
It makes new living things.
items.explanation: Animals have babies and plants make seeds. This is how living things reproduce.

items.prompt: Which shows that a living thing can sense its surroundings?

options.text: A snail pulls in its horns when touched.

options.why: A rock is not alive.
A candle is not alive.

options.text: A cloud moves across the sky.
options.why: A cloud is not alive.

hints: Look for something that reacts.
Only living things react like this.
Rocks and clouds do not feel.
items.explanation: The snail feels the touch and pulls in its horns. This shows it is sensitive.

items.prompt: A mushroom pops up after rain and grows bigger. What is it?

options.why: It is growing now.
It grows, so it is alive.
Rocks do not grow.

hints: It grows bigger.
Rocks do not grow.
Things that grow are alive.
items.explanation: Mushrooms grow, so they are alive. They are not plants or animals but are living things called fungi.

items.prompt: Alive, once alive or never alive? Sort the cards.
hints: Wood comes from trees.
Wool comes from sheep.
Stone and glass come from the ground.
items.explanation: A frog and an oak tree are alive now. A table, a wool jumper and a leather shoe came from living things. Stone and glass were never alive.

items.prompt: Choose all the living things.
hints: Ask: does it grow and need food?
A wooden spoon was part of a tree.
Rivers flow but do not grow.
items.explanation: A fern, a mushroom and a spider are alive. A wooden spoon was once alive but is not alive now. Clouds and rivers were never alive.

items.prompt: Choose all the things that were once alive.
hints: Wood comes from trees.
Leather comes from animals.
Rocks were never alive.
items.explanation: Wood, cotton and leather come from plants and animals. Metal, stone and glass come from the ground.

items.prompt: Match each object to where it came from.
hints: Wool is the hair of sheep.
Leather is animal skin.
Wood is from trees.
items.explanation: A chair comes from a tree and a jumper comes from a sheep. A shirt comes from a cotton plant and a shoe comes from a cow.

items.prompt: Living things need food, ___ and air. They ___ bigger as they get older.
hints: What do you drink?
A puppy gets bigger.
Say the sentence out loud.
items.explanation: Living things need food, water and air. They grow bigger as they get older.

items.prompt: Alive, once alive or never alive?
head: Thing
Type
hints: A bench is made of wood.
A stone never grew.
A mushroom grows.
items.explanation: A tiger and a mushroom are alive. A wooden bench was once alive. A stone was never alive.

items.prompt: Tara finds a log in the woods. Mushrooms grow on the log. A beetle crawls over it. The log is dry and does not grow.
hints: Which things grow or move?
The log does not grow.
Logs come from trees.
items.explanation: The mushrooms and the beetle are alive. The log came from a tree.

items.prompt: How many living things are in the picture?

figure.alt: A dog, a tree, a bee, a rock and a mushroom.

hints: Count only living things.
A mushroom is alive.
A chair is not alive.
items.explanation: The dog, the tree, the bee and the mushroom are alive. The chair and the rock are not.

items.prompt: Tap the thing that was never alive.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: rock, tree, frog and bee.

hints: Which one has never grown?
Trees and frogs are alive.
It is hard and grey.
items.explanation: A rock was never alive. A tree, a frog and a bee are alive.

items.prompt: Tap the two things that were once alive.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: wooden spoon, rock, glass and paper.

hints: What is wood made from?
What is paper made from?
Glass comes from sand.
items.explanation: A wooden spoon and paper are made from trees, which were alive. Rock and glass were never alive.

items.prompt: Put the life of a tree in order.
hints: A seed comes first.
The tree is tall.
A log is last.
items.explanation: A tree begins as a seed. It grows into a seedling and then a tall tree. When it dies it can become a log.

items.prompt: A rock was never ___.
hints: Does a rock grow?
Rocks do not eat.
It starts with a.
items.explanation: A rock is a non-living thing. It was never alive.

items.prompt: Which group has only living things?

options.text: a fern, a frog, a rock
options.why: A rock is not alive.

options.text: a fish, a car, a tree
options.why: A car is not alive.

options.text: a frog, a spoon, a bee
options.why: A spoon is not alive.

options.text: a fern, a frog, a fish

hints: Check each thing in the group.
One wrong thing makes the group wrong.
Rocks and cars never grow.
items.explanation: A fern, a frog and a fish are all alive.

items.prompt: Which is the odd one out?

figure.alt: A wooden spoon, paper, glass and a feather.

options.why: It was once alive.
It was once alive.
It was once alive.

hints: Which came from the ground?
Wood comes from trees.
A feather comes from a bird.
items.explanation: Wood, paper and a feather all came from living things. Glass was never alive.

items.prompt: Raj says a flame is alive. It moves and needs air. Which shows he is wrong?

options.why: Being hot does not decide it.
Being bright does not decide it.

options.text: A flame does not eat or have babies.

options.why: Size does not decide it.

hints: Think about all the life processes.
Hot or bright does not matter.
Living things feed and reproduce.
items.explanation: A flame moves and needs air. But it does not grow, eat or have babies like a living thing.
